title: Wanzhu
synopsis: Learn about the leisure activities of old Beijingers.

fullText.simplified:
玩主

    “玩主”，北京方言，它是一种京味儿文化。被叫做“玩主”的人把玩儿当成正经事，玩出了很多花样。
    老北京人好玩儿，擅玩儿。今天就给大家介绍几种老北京人常玩的物品。
    首先就是“核桃”。有句老话：核桃不离手，活过八十九。其实这句话表达的就是北京人对核桃的一种喜爱。在北京，你经常能看到手里拿着一对核桃，顺时针或者逆时针转动核桃的人，而且转的时候一定要出声，就是两个核桃转动发出的摩擦声。玩核桃的愿意听那个响声，觉得好听，让人心情愉悦。
    其次是“手串儿”。很多北京爷们儿手腕上都会戴着一串手串儿，大多是木质的。没事儿的时候，他们就会用手或者刷子摩擦手串，这个过程就叫“盘”。时间久了以后，木头手串儿就会显得油亮有光泽了。据说盘串既可以改善皮肤状况又能缓解压力。
    最后，要介绍的是“玩鸟儿”。天气好的时候，如果你走在北京的大街上或者逛北京的胡同，经常能看到遛鸟儿的大爷或者门口挂着鸟笼的院子。玩鸟儿的人常常把鸟笼挂在公园的树上，让小鸟们熟悉大自然的声音，然后跟养鸟的朋友交流经验，或者向别人展示一下训鸟的成果。
    不管是玩核桃、盘手串儿还是玩鸟儿，都是对老北京文化的一种体现，也从另外一个层面体现了老北京人休闲惬意的生活状态。
fullText.traditional:
玩主

    “玩主”，北京方言，它是一種京味兒文化。被叫做“玩主”的人把玩兒當成正經事，玩出了很多花樣。
    老北京人好玩兒，擅玩兒。今天就給大家介紹幾種老北京人常玩的物品。
    首先就是“核桃”。有句老話：核桃不離手，活過八十九。其實這句話表達的就是北京人對核桃的一種喜愛。在北京，你經常能看到手裡拿著一對核桃，順時針或者逆時針轉動核桃的人，而且轉的時候一定要出聲，就是兩個核桃轉動發出的摩擦聲。玩核桃的願意聽那個響聲，覺得好聽，讓人心情愉悅。
    其次是“手串兒”。很多北京爺們兒手腕上都會戴著一串手串兒，大多是木質的。沒事兒的時候，他們就會用手或者刷子摩擦手串，這個過程就叫“盤”。時間久了以後，木頭手串兒就會顯得油亮有光澤了。據說盤串既可以改善皮膚狀況又能緩解壓力。
    最後，要介紹的是“玩鳥兒”。天氣好的時候，如果你走在北京的大街上或者逛北京的胡同，經常能看到遛鳥兒的大爺或者門口掛著鳥籠的院子。玩鳥兒的人常常把鳥籠掛在公園的樹上，讓小鳥們熟悉大自然的聲音，然後跟養鳥的朋友交流經驗，或者向別人展示一下訓鳥的成果。
    不管是玩核桃、盤手串兒還是玩鳥兒，都是對老北京文化的一種體現，也從另外一個層面體現了老北京人休閒愜意的生活狀態。

sentences.simplified: “玩主”，北京方言，它是一种京味儿文化。
sentences.traditional: “玩主”，北京方言，它是一種京味兒文化。
sentences.pinyin: wán zhǔ běi jīng fāng yán tā shì yì zhǒng jīng wèi'r wén huà

sentences.simplified: 被叫做“玩主”的人把玩儿当成正经事，玩出了很多花样。
sentences.traditional: 被叫做“玩主”的人把玩兒當成正經事，玩出了很多花樣。
sentences.pinyin: bèi jiào zuò wán zhǔ de rén bǎ wán'r dāng chéng zhèng jīng shì wán chū le hěn duō huā yàng
sentences.english: In the Beijing dialect, “wanzhu” refers to a certain type of Beijing culture.
People who are called “wanzhu” consider playing a serious business and play in many different ways.

sentences.simplified: 老北京人好玩儿，擅玩儿。
sentences.traditional: 老北京人好玩兒，擅玩兒。
sentences.pinyin: lǎo běi jīng rén hào wán'r shàn wán'r

sentences.simplified: 今天就给大家介绍几种老北京人常玩的物品。
sentences.traditional: 今天就給大家介紹幾種老北京人常玩的物品。

sentences.english: Old Beijingers like to play and are good at playing.
Today we will give everyone an introduction to some of the things that old Beijingers often play with.

sentences.simplified: 首先就是“核桃”。有句老话：核桃不离手，活过八十九。
sentences.traditional: 首先就是“核桃”。有句老話：核桃不離手，活過八十九。

sentences.traditional: 其實這句話表達的就是北京人對核桃的一種喜愛。
sentences.pinyin: qí shí zhè jù huà biǎo dá de jiù shì běi jīng rén duì hé tao de yì zhǒng xǐ ài
sentences.english: The first is “walnuts”. There is an old saying: If walnuts never leave your hand, you will live past 89.

sentences.simplified: 在北京，你经常能看到手里拿着一对核桃，
sentences.traditional: 在北京，你經常能看到手裡拿著一對核桃，
sentences.pinyin: zài běi jīng nǐ jīng cháng néng kàn dào shǒu lǐ ná zhe yí duì hé tao
sentences.english: In fact, this phrase expresses Beijingers’ love for walnuts.

sentences.simplified: 顺时针或者逆时针转动核桃的人，
sentences.traditional: 順時針或者逆時針轉動核桃的人，
sentences.pinyin: shùn shí zhēn huò zhě nì shí zhēn zhuàn dòng hé tao de rén
sentences.english: In Beijing, you can often see people holding a couple of walnuts in their hands, ..

sentences.simplified: 而且转的时候一定要出声，就是两个核桃转动发出的摩擦声。
sentences.traditional: 而且轉的時候一定要出聲，就是兩個核桃轉動發出的摩擦聲。
sentences.pinyin: ér qiě zhuàn de shí hou yí dìng yào chū shēng jiù shì liǎng ge hé tao zhuàn dòng fā chū de mó cā shēng
sentences.english: .. turning them either clockwise or counterclockwise.

sentences.simplified: 玩核桃的愿意听那个响声，觉得好听，让人心情愉悦。
sentences.traditional: 玩核桃的願意聽那個響聲，覺得好聽，讓人心情愉悅。
sentences.pinyin: wán hé tao de yuàn yì tīng nà ge xiǎng shēng jué de hǎo tīng ràng rén xīn qíng yú yuè
sentences.english: The walnuts should make a sound when they are turned. That is the sound of the rubbing of walnuts.
Those who play with walnuts want to listen to that sound. They think it sounds nice and it makes people happy.

sentences.simplified: 其次是“手串儿”。
sentences.traditional: 其次是“手串兒”。

sentences.english: The next one is “beaded bracelets”.

sentences.simplified: 没事儿的时候，他们就会用手或者刷子摩擦手串，这个过程就叫“盘”。
sentences.traditional: 沒事兒的時候，他們就會用手或者刷子摩擦手串，這個過程就叫“盤”。
sentences.pinyin: méi shì'r de shí hou tā men jiù huì yòng shǒu huò zhě shuā zi mó cā shǒu chuàn zhè ge guò chéng jiù jiào pán
sentences.english: Many Beijing men wear a beaded bracelet on their wrist, usually made of wood.

sentences.simplified: 时间久了以后，木头手串儿就会显得油亮有光泽了。

sentences.english: When they have nothing to do, they use their hands or a brush to rub the bracelet. This process is called “pan”.

sentences.simplified: 据说盘串既可以改善皮肤状况又能缓解压力。
sentences.traditional: 據說盤串既可以改善皮膚狀況又能緩解壓力。

It is said that rubbing the bracelet can both improve your skin condition and alleviate stress.

sentences.simplified: 最后，要介绍的是“玩鸟儿”。
sentences.traditional: 最後，要介紹的是“玩鳥兒”。
sentences.pinyin: zuì hòu yào jiè shào de shì wán niǎo'r

sentences.english: Finally, I would like to introduce “playing with birds”.

sentences.simplified: 经常能看到遛鸟儿的大爷或者门口挂着鸟笼的院子。

sentences.english: If you walk along the streets of Beijing or stroll through Beijing’s hutongs when the weather is good, ..

sentences.simplified: 玩鸟儿的人常常把鸟笼挂在公园的树上，让小鸟们熟悉大自然的声音，
sentences.traditional: 玩鳥兒的人常常把鳥籠掛在公園的樹上，讓小鳥們熟悉大自然的聲音，
sentences.pinyin: wán niǎo'r de rén cháng cháng bǎ niǎo lóng guà zài gōng yuán de shù shang ràng xiǎo niǎo men shú xī dà zì rán de shēng yīn
sentences.english: .. you can often see old men walking their birds or courtyards with bird cages hanging at the gate.

sentences.simplified: 然后跟养鸟的朋友交流经验，或者向别人展示一下训鸟的成果。
sentences.traditional: 然後跟養鳥的朋友交流經驗，或者向別人展示一下訓鳥的成果。
sentences.pinyin: rán hòu gēn yǎng niǎo de péng you jiāo liú jīng yàn huò zhě xiàng bié ren zhǎn shì yí xià xùn niǎo de chéng guǒ
sentences.english: People who play with birds often hang birdcages on trees in parks to make the birds familiar with the sounds of nature.
Then they share their experiences looking after birds with friends or show others the results of their bird training.

sentences.simplified: 也从另外一个层面体现了老北京人休闲惬意的生活状态。
sentences.traditional: 也從另外一個層面體現了老北京人休閒愜意的生活狀態。
sentences.pinyin: yě cóng lìng wài yí ge céng miàn tǐ xiàn le lǎo běi jīng rén xiū xián qiè yì de shēng huó zhuàng tài
sentences.english: Whether it’s playing with walnuts, rubbing beads, or playing with birds, these are embodiments of old Beijing culture.

sentence_translations: Wanzhu
In the Beijing dialect, “wanzhu” refers to a certain type of Beijing culture.
People who are called “wanzhu” consider playing a serious business and play in many different ways.
Old Beijingers like to play and are good at playing.
Today we will give everyone an introduction to some of the things that old Beijingers often play with.
The first is “walnuts”. There is an old saying: If walnuts never leave your hand, you will live past 89.
In fact, this phrase expresses Beijingers’ love for walnuts.
In Beijing, you can often see people holding a couple of walnuts in their hands, ..
.. turning them either clockwise or counterclockwise.
The walnuts should make a sound when they are turned. That is the sound of the rubbing of walnuts.
Those who play with walnuts want to listen to that sound. They think it sounds nice and it makes people happy.
The next one is “beaded bracelets”.
Many Beijing men wear a beaded bracelet on their wrist, usually made of wood.
When they have nothing to do, they use their hands or a brush to rub the bracelet. This process is called “pan”.
After a long time, the wooden bracelet will look shiny and glossy.
It is said that rubbing the bracelet can both improve your skin condition and alleviate stress.
Finally, I would like to introduce “playing with birds”.
If you walk along the streets of Beijing or stroll through Beijing’s hutongs when the weather is good, ..
.. you can often see old men walking their birds or courtyards with bird cages hanging at the gate.
People who play with birds often hang birdcages on trees in parks to make the birds familiar with the sounds of nature.
Then they share their experiences looking after birds with friends or show others the results of their bird training.
Whether it’s playing with walnuts, rubbing beads, or playing with birds, these are embodiments of old Beijing culture.
On another level, they also reflect the leisurely and agreeable lives of old Beijingers.
